title: Best Time to Visit Bali, Thailand, Vietnam and Sri Lanka: Month by Month
metaDescription: A month-by-month guide to the best time to visit Southeast Asia and Sri Lanka, covering monsoon patterns, shoulder seasons and where to go in each month.
excerpt: Southeast Asia does not have one season. It has several overlapping monsoons, which means there is always somewhere good to be.
author: Travel Editors
content:
"When is the best time to go to Southeast Asia?" has no single answer, because the region does not share a climate. Monsoons arrive at different times in different places, and in some countries two coasts a hundred kilometres apart have opposite seasons.

The useful version of the question is: **in the month I can travel, where should I go?** Here is that answer, country by country and then month by month.

## The Monsoon Basics

Two systems dominate:

- **The southwest monsoon**, roughly May to October, brings rain to Thailand's Andaman coast, Sri Lanka's west and south, and much of mainland Southeast Asia
- **The northeast monsoon**, roughly November to March, brings rain to Thailand's Gulf coast, Sri Lanka's east and north, and central Vietnam

Which is why Thailand and Sri Lanka always have a good coast — it just moves.

A note on what "rainy season" means: outside a few genuinely severe months, tropical rain is typically an intense afternoon downpour for an hour or two, not all-day drizzle. Travel remains entirely feasible, prices drop substantially, and landscapes are at their greenest. The real risks are sea conditions affecting boat transport and, in some places, flooding.

## Thailand

- **November to February** — the best overall. Dry, cooler, and peak season everywhere. Book ahead
- **March to May** — very hot, up to 40°C inland. Songkran in mid-April is worth experiencing. Northern Thailand has significant agricultural burning haze in March and April
- **June to October** — wet season on the Andaman coast (Phuket, Krabi). The **Gulf islands** — Samui, Phangan, Tao — have their driest weather in this window, which is the single most useful fact about Thailand's climate
- **October and November** — the Gulf's wettest months. Reverse of the Andaman

**In short:** Andaman coast November to April, Gulf coast June to September.

![Southeast Asia travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1602646993875-70bc0ba52c87?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## Vietnam

Vietnam is 1,600 kilometres long and has three distinct climates.

- **North (Hanoi, Sapa, Ha Long)** — best October to December and March to April. Cold and drizzly January and February; hot and wet June to August
- **Central (Hue, Hoi An, Da Nang)** — best February to May. September to November brings the heaviest rain and occasional typhoons
- **South (Ho Chi Minh City, Mekong, Phu Quoc)** — dry December to April, wet May to November
- **The best window for the whole country** — **February to April**

Avoid **Tet**, the lunar new year, unless it is the reason you are going: much of the country closes and transport sells out.

## Bali and Indonesia

- **April to October** — the dry season, and the best time. June to September is peak
- **November to March** — the wet season. Humid, with heavy afternoon rain. Prices fall; the rice terraces are spectacular
- **April, May and October** — the sweet spots: dry weather, lower prices, fewer people
- **Note** — Bali is busy in July and August and around Christmas, with genuine traffic problems in the Canggu–Seminyak corridor

**Nusa Penida, the Gilis and Lombok** follow the same pattern. **Raja Ampat** and eastern Indonesia differ — best roughly October to April.

## Sri Lanka

The most confusing and the most forgiving, because there is always a good half of the island.

- **December to March** — the west and south coasts (Colombo, Galle, Mirissa, Bentota) and the cultural triangle at their best. Peak season
- **May to September** — the **east coast** (Arugam Bay, Trincomalee, Pasikudah) at its best. Surf season in Arugam Bay
- **The hill country** (Kandy, Ella, Nuwara Eliya) — reasonable year-round, wettest October to December
- **The shoulder months of April and September** — inter-monsoon, less predictable, but often genuinely good across the whole island with very few visitors

**Whale watching:** Mirissa in the south from December to April; Trincomalee in the east from May to September.

![Southeast Asia travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1537953773345-d172ccf13cf1?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## Month by Month: Where to Go

**January** — Thailand's Andaman coast, southern Vietnam, Sri Lanka's south and west, Cambodia, Laos. Peak season, peak prices, best weather.

**February** — The best month for Vietnam end to end. Also excellent: Thailand, Sri Lanka's south, the Philippines, Myanmar.

**March** — Vietnam still good. Thailand getting hot. Sri Lanka's south good. Avoid northern Thailand and Laos for burning-season haze.

**April** — Bali's dry season begins with low crowds. Sri Lanka inter-monsoon. Songkran in Thailand. Vietnam's central coast at its best. Very hot in mainland Southeast Asia.

**May** — Bali excellent. Thailand's Gulf islands begin their good season. Sri Lanka's east coast opens. Shoulder pricing across the region.

**June** — Bali, the Gulf islands, Sri Lanka's east coast, and northern Vietnam's mountains. Andaman coast wet.

**July** — Peak in Bali and the Gulf islands. Sri Lanka's east. Busy and more expensive.

**August** — Same as July, plus European school holidays adding pressure. Book well ahead.

**September** — One of the best value months. Bali quiet and still dry, Gulf islands good, Sri Lanka's east still open, and the whole region cheaper. Central Vietnam entering its wet season.

**October** — Bali at the end of its dry season with very few people. Northern Vietnam excellent. Thailand transitional. Sri Lanka inter-monsoon.

**November** — Thailand's Andaman coast reopens with excellent weather and pre-peak prices. Northern Vietnam excellent. One of the single best months in the region.

**December** — Peak everywhere in the dry zones. Excellent weather, highest prices, book months ahead. Sri Lanka's south, Thailand's Andaman, southern Vietnam.

## The Practical Takeaways

**There is no bad month for Southeast Asia.** There is a bad combination of month and destination, and it is entirely avoidable.

**The best value months are May, September and October** — shoulder periods with good weather somewhere, substantially lower prices, and far fewer people.

**The most expensive weeks are Christmas and New Year**, everywhere, by a wide margin. Book five to eight months ahead or travel in January instead.

**Always check the regional pattern, not the national one.** "Thailand in July" is meaningless. "Koh Samui in July" is excellent and "Phuket in July" is wet.

**Wet season is underrated.** Half-price accommodation, empty beaches, green landscapes and afternoon rain you can plan around. The exception is where boat transport matters — island hopping in a wet season means cancelled ferries.

If you are planning around a fixed set of dates rather than a fixed destination, the question inverts usefully: put your available weeks down first, then choose the region that is at its best then. Laying the candidate destinations against your dates in **Trypinn** makes that comparison concrete, and it usually produces a better trip than starting from a destination and hoping the weather cooperates.
